thread.title: Jerdy Lopez named to Brooks Wallace Award watch list for top collegiate shortstop
thread.title_full: Jerdy Lopez named to Brooks Wallace Award watch list for top collegiate shortstop

author: m. h. stevenson
title: Jerdy Lopez named to Brooks Wallace Award watch list for top collegiate shortstop
text:
Little Rock shortstop Jerdy Lopez has been named to the 2026 Brooks Wallace Player of the Year Award Watch List, which recognizes the top collegiate shortstop in the nation. The award is presented annually by the College Baseball Foundation.
Head coach Chris Curry commented on Lopez’s recognition: “We are proud that Jerdy has been named to this prestigious watch list. Jerdy works very hard and helps our team tremendously as a plus defender.”
Lopez, originally from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, transferred from Western Oklahoma CC and has started all 12 games for the Trojans this season. He has accumulated eight hits, three runs batted in, two stolen bases, and maintained a perfect fielding percentage across 44 chances while contributing to eight double plays.
The initial list features 100 shortstops nationwide. While offensive performance is considered, defensive skills are also important for inclusion. Larry Wallace, co-chair of the Brooks Wallace Award, said: “Our staff is excited to get another year started looking for that special player to represent Brooks’ Award. We will dig deep to find the personal qualities as well as the physical attributes that best exemplify what we look for in the Brooks Wallace Award winner. It’s early, but this list is already shaping up to be a competitive race with some big numbers from some new faces and some familiar names as well.”
The College Baseball Foundation also presents other honors including the John Olerud Two-Way Player Award, National Pitcher of the Week Award, and Buster Posey Collegiate Catcher of the Week Award.
Chris Snead, CBF Awards Chair, stated: “With the season now in full swing, there are so many deserving candidates for our many awards. This is just the beginning of this process that culminates with our announcements in Omaha.”
More information about these awards can be found at the College Baseball Foundation website at www.collegebaseballhall.org .
